standard.title: Plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts
standard.description: plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts whose purposes may be imaginative, informative and persuasive, using paragraphs, a variety of complex sentences, expanded verb groups, tense, topic-specific and vivid vocabulary, punctuation, spelling and visual features
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts across imaginative, informative and persuasive purposes, using paragraphs, complex sentences, expanded noun and verb groups, tense, vocabulary choices, punctuation and spelling (AC9E5LY06). They have not yet specifically deployed embedded clauses, elaborated tenses, adverb groups, or explicitly rhetorical devices in their writing.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts for imaginative, informative and persuasive purposes, using paragraphs, complex sentences (including embedded clauses), expanded verb groups, tense, topic-specific and vivid vocabulary, appropriate punctuation and spelling, and visual features.

nodes.label: Planning for purpose and audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a written or multimodal text that identifies the purpose, audience, text structure and key language choices to be made.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a plan for a written text identifying purpose, intended audience, text structure, and at least two key language choices (e.g. vocabulary register, sentence type) suited to that purpose and audience.
nodes.typical_width: Plan texts for imaginative, informative and persuasive purposes with attention to audience; identify text structure, vocabulary register, language features and visual elements appropriate to purpose and audience; note how the plan will use language choices taught in the Language strand.
wider: Plan the same text for two different audiences (e.g. a persuasive text for peers and for a council), identifying what language choices would differ
Plan a multimodal text and evaluate how digital tools and visual elements will work alongside the written text to serve purpose
success_criteria: Produces a plan that identifies purpose, audience and text structure
Identifies at least two language choices appropriate to the purpose and audience

nodes.label: Creating with varied complex sentences and precise vocabulary
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create written texts that deploy a variety of complex sentences (including embedded clauses), expanded verb groups, tense choices, and topic-specific and vivid vocabulary.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a paragraph that includes at least one embedded clause, at least one precise verb choice, and vocabulary appropriate to the text's purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Create written texts that use a variety of complex sentences including embedded clauses; use expanded verb groups, appropriate tense, topic-specific and vivid vocabulary; use rhetorical devices, images and modal verbs for persuasive effects where relevant.
wider: Create an informative text for two different audiences, adjusting text structure and language choices for each, and note the changes required
Use digital tools to combine written and multimodal elements, evaluating how the combination serves the purpose

response_modes.reason: Writing with embedded clauses, precise vocabulary, tense control and vivid language simultaneously requires integrating the conceptual knowledge from multiple LA strand descriptors into a coherent production act — the integration is the learning challenge.

success_criteria: Produces a paragraph that includes at least one embedded clause and at least one precise verb choice
Uses vocabulary that is appropriate to the purpose and audience of the text

nodes.label: Editing for structure, meaning and accuracy
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can re-read and edit their own and others' work against negotiated criteria for text structure, meaning, grammar, spelling and punctuation, and explain editing choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Re-read own writing and make at least two edits against a stated criterion (e.g. punctuation accuracy, vocabulary precision); explain at least one editing choice.
nodes.typical_width: Re-read and edit own and others' work using negotiated criteria across text structure, meaning, accuracy of grammar, spelling and punctuation; explain editing choices; use knowledge of comma rules, embedded clauses and word choice to improve writing.
wider: Edit a provided piece of writing against multiple criteria and write a brief editor's note explaining each significant change and why it improves the text
Use the editing process to deliberately introduce a literary device and evaluate whether it improves the text

response_modes.reason: Editing accuracy — particularly comma use, embedded clause structure and spelling — requires repeated practice to become reliable. Students who understand the rules conceptually still need editing practice to apply them consistently under production pressure.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Editing against multiple criteria and explaining choices is genuinely rich metacognitive work — it develops authorial agency and the language for discussing writing choices that carries into secondary English.
success_criteria: Makes at least two edits to a piece of writing and identifies what criterion each addresses
Explains at least one editing choice in terms of how it improves the text's purpose, meaning or accuracy
